title: Sleep Trackers May Make You Feel More Tired
paragraphs: You're getting ready for bed. You've taken your magnesium, turned on the white noise machine, put on your sleep mask, and checked that your sleep tracker is working.
Routines like this have become increasingly common as part of "sleepmaxxing" — a trend focused on trying different products and techniques to get the best possible night's sleep.
Being more aware of the importance of high-quality sleep is certainly a good thing, as sleep plays a crucial role in both our physical and mental health.
But experts warn that obsessing over perfect sleep can backfire. And sleep trackers may be exacerbating the problem.
Researchers have even coined a term for this: "orthosomnia" — an unhealthy obsession with achieving optimal sleep, often driven by sleep tracker data.
A 2026 study found that a third of US adults used digital tools to track their sleep, and 31% of those users showed signs of orthosomnia risk.

Part of the problem is that sleep trackers aren't completely accurate. Rather than measuring brain activity, sleep trackers use information such as movement and heart rate to estimate whether a person is asleep.
"If you want to measure sleep, you have to measure the brain," sleep expert Neil Stanley recently told the BBC.
Consumer devices can have trouble differentiating between sleep stages, or even between being asleep and simply lying in bed awake. And those imperfect numbers could have a powerful effect.

In one study from the University of Oxford, researchers used watches to give participants random information about how well they had slept. Those who were told they had slept badly reported feeling more tired and less alert the next day — even though the data was completely made up.

Rather than worrying about tracker results, experts recommend just creating the right conditions for good sleep: make your bedroom reasonably cool, dark and quiet; get bright light in the morning; exercise regularly; and eat a healthy diet.
And if you wake up feeling rested and ready for the day, a disappointing number on your wrist isn't worth losing sleep over!
